findings.description: This subnet assigns public IPv4 addresses by default and is associated with an Internet-gateway default route. Workloads launched here can be Internet-reachable if their security groups permit ingress.

This subnet assigns public IPv4 addresses by default and is associated with an Internet-gateway default route. The portal server is launched here, giving it public network reachability in combination with its security group.
The EBS volume does not explicitly enable encryption. Its data can be stored unencrypted unless encryption is imposed by an external account-level default.

User data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. These credentials can be exposed through source control, Terraform state, logs, or instance/user-data access and permit use of the associated IAM principal's permissions.
The security group permits TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0 and is attached to an instance with public addressing in an Internet-routable subnet, exposing SSH to arbitrary Internet sources.
The bucket that stores VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Flow-log data may therefore be stored without encryption at rest unless an external account policy enforces it.
